record.context_brief: Avoiding sparse forbidden entries in Latin squares
record.original_question: Let A be an n×n array with entries from {0,...,n} such that each nonzero symbol appears in at most n−2 positions. Must there always exist a Latin square L on symbols {1,...,n} such that L_{i,j}≠A_{i,j} for every cell?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10.7. For any A there exists a latin square L, using the symbols {1, . . . , n} such Li,j 6= Ai,j

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ be an integer. An $n\times n$ array $A=(A_{i,j})$ has entries from $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$, where the entry $0$ is regarded as "blank". Assume that for every symbol $s\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, the number of cells $(i,j)$ with $A_{i,j}=s$ is at most $n-2$.

A Latin square of order $n$ on the symbol set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is an $n\times n$ array $L=(L_{i,j})$ with $L_{i,j}\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ such that every symbol occurs exactly once in each row and exactly once in each column.

Prove or disprove: for every such array $A$ there exists a Latin square $L$ of order $n$ on $\{1,\dots,n\}$ with $L_{i,j}\ne A_{i,j}$ for all $i,j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is a strong form of Häggkvist-type avoidability for Latin squares. Known results establish avoidability under stronger sparsity hypotheses (e.g., each symbol occurs at most cn times in each row and each column, for a small constant c, and analogous results for arrays of odd order), but the exact threshold "each symbol appears at most n−2 times in total" does not appear to be established. No source found that fully resolves the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Avoiding Arrays of Odd Order by Latin Squares
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes avoidability for odd-order arrays under density bounds of the form cn, leaving stronger forms open.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for sparse avoidability, but not the n−2 form.

status_evidence.title: On Latin squares and avoidable arrays
status_evidence.snippet: Thesis surveying results and open problems on avoidable arrays by Latin squares.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture on avoiding arrays remains open in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Restricted completion of sparse partial Latin squares
status_evidence.snippet: Treats sparse arrays with each symbol appearing at most βn times under small β.
status_evidence.claim: Available results require strictly stronger sparsity than n−2 occurrences.
